parallel.requirements: The parallel attempt recognized the clean-room replacement requirement, the ban on source lookup and binary analysis, and broad `xz` CLI surface including help, version, compression, decompression, list, aliases, raw and `.lzma` behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent spawned children for probing but both parent and children became implementation owners, producing competing source files and build-script edits rather than a single isolated ownership plan.
parallel.implementation: The final parent implementation was `src/cleanxz.py`, while children also produced `src/xz_reimpl.py` and `src/xz_clone.py`; the final artifact retained multiple competing implementations.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivery went through `compile.sh` and `./executable`, but live agents replaced that build path during validation, requiring inspection and restoration attempts before finalization.
parallel.verification: The parent ran representative self-checks and final smoke tests, and children performed extensive CLI probes, but final verification occurred after an unstable deliverable path had been observed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The current official evaluation failed despite a high evaluated-test pass rate; the final response identified advanced tuning and memlimit semantics as lower-confidence areas.

serial.requirements: The serial attempt recognized the same clean-room constraints and focused on observed `xz 5.8.2` behavior, including manual `.xz`, `.lzma`, stdin/stdout, suffix, overwrite, list, verbose, robot, help, version, and info-memory paths.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned probing, implementation, build, validation, cleanup, and final delivery without delegation or parallel subagent work.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote a single implementation, `src/xz_reimplementation.py`, plus one `compile.sh` that installed it as `./executable`.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial build path stayed coherent: compile script copied the single source file to the executable target and the reference copy was removed before finalization.
serial.verification: The serial run validated byte-for-byte and exit-code behavior on a broad representative matrix, including compression presets, block size, list variants, suffixes, stdin, and error paths.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The current official evaluation also failed; the final response explicitly left advanced filter-chain and non-`xz`/`lzma` formats such as `lzip` and `raw` unimplemented.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the clean-room executable task and broad `xz`/`.lzma`/raw CLI behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same clean-room task and broad observed `xz 5.8.2` CLI surface.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both saw the same benchmark obligations; the difference is not a missed prompt requirement but execution and delivered surface coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used multi-agent fan-out with several child threads, but implementation ownership overlapped across parent and children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial disabled multi-agent features and one actor owned probing through delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained more simultaneous probing and implementation work but created competing implementation ownership; serial was slower in breadth but coherent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had no stable cross-agent contract for which source and compile script owned the deliverable path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial maintained a single source-to-build interface from implementation to executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material interface difference was not a lost handoff but live disagreement over the required build entry point.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel final delivery used `src/cleanxz.py`, while child implementations `src/xz_reimpl.py` and `src/xz_clone.py` also remained in the artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial delivery used the single `src/xz_reimplementation.py` path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced more competing code paths; serial produced one coherent path with a clearer provenance chain.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: A child interrupted another active child after deciding to restore its own build path, and the parent later finalized independently.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join and closed after updating its plan and final smoke checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had active child lifecycle interference around competing work; serial had a linear local result lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel agents wrote and rewrote `compile.sh` and `./executable` in the shared workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one build script and one executable target without a concurrent writer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the central concurrency difference: parallel had a realized shared-state deliverable overwrite, serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel reported representative checks after building `./executable`, while noting unexhausted advanced tuning semantics.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reported a broader reference-comparison matrix but still admitted advanced filter and format gaps.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified representative cases and both left advanced behavior uncertain; parallel verification also had to contend with a disputed executable target.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used subagents and substantial tool calls, then closed with a final implementation after reconciliation and self-checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no delegation and closed after a single implementation and validation cycle.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's budget pressure included coordination and reconciliation overhead, but it still completed the final response; serial spent the budget on one path.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation gives `both_fail`: parallel passed 1211 of 1263 evaluated tests and serial passed 1117 of 1263 evaluated tests, with both `solution_passed` values false. Parallel materially outscored serial, likely because its final `cleanxz.py` covered some additional observed surface, but the official pass/fail outcome is not discordant. The retained parallel write pattern is an adverse coordination process issue, not a proven explanation for a pass/fail difference.
parallel_contributors: Parallel delivered `src/cleanxz.py` and claimed observed `xz`, `.lzma`, and raw behavior, but also had competing implementations and deliverable overwrite/reconciliation overhead.
serial_contributors: Serial kept one coherent implementation and build path but final text acknowledged advanced filter-chain and non-`xz`/`lzma` formats were not implemented.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts failed hidden official coverage despite representative self-tests.
Parallel scored higher on evaluated tests, while serial explicitly omitted `lzip` and `raw` formats.
evaluator_effects: Original evaluation summaries timed out; the completed retry evaluation in `cell/status.json` supersedes them.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative explanation with no pass/fail outcome difference

candidates.reason: Implementation was not ownerless: parent and children each actively produced implementations; the problem was overlapping ownership and overwrite, not absence of an implementer.
Integration was not unowned; agents repeatedly inspected and modified the shared build path. The concrete adverse event was deliverable replacement.
Final assembly had active owners through `compile.sh` and `./executable`; the retained issue is that multiple owners overwrote the same deliverable.
The parent continued through implementation, build, checks, and final delivery. The failure mode is not an unowned end-to-end pipeline.
Productive implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory preflight; parent and children implemented while probes were ongoing.
The parallel run did not complete all investigation before deferring implementation; implementation overlapped with probing in multiple actors.
The indispensable implementation path had active capacity in parent and children; the adverse evidence is a write collision, not underallocation of the critical path.
There was fan-out and a failed spawn, but no distinct collective fan-out budget exhaustion episode independent of the live deliverable overwrite chain.
Children overproduced implementations, but the record does not show one overbroad child assignment whose unfinished scope uniquely caused the adverse result.
Children were initially probe-oriented, but the retained consequence came from live shared deliverable writes, not from a known task requirement omitted from a child brief.
A missing file-owner contract is plausible background, but the taxonomy says to use the concrete write label when live agents collide or overwrite the deliverable.
No known finding or current-file fact is shown disappearing through a handoff and causing repeated work; the contested state was visible in the shared workspace.
Child reports contained detail, but no returned handoff was too large or unstructured for the parent to consume before closure.
No receiver relied on a transferred report that was stale relative to a newer visible workspace state; the issue was direct concurrent workspace modification.
There were conflicting implementation paths, but the conflict manifested as file and deliverable writes rather than incompatible returned handoffs left unadjudicated.
The parent ran final self-checks and explicitly noted lower-confidence areas; hidden evaluator failure alone cannot establish an unsupported acceptance decision.
No replacement or retry was delegated without inherited checkpoints and then repeated prior work; implementation competition occurred live in one shared attempt.

candidates.reason: A child interrupted another running child, but that interruption is downstream of the same deliverable overwrite chain and did not leave a separate required result unfinished.
Usable candidate implementations were not merely left unpromoted; the final build path was actively overwritten and reconciled, making the write label more specific.
No child result is shown being merged only after integrated verification without recheck; final checks occurred after the parent-selected deliverable path.
Child implementations were not cleanly joined, but the concrete adverse boundary is live replacement of the required build entry point rather than a completed delegated implementation simply ignored.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding trapped below the parent; available child findings and workspace state were visible.
Interrupted or failed child work did not leave a separate required scope abandoned; the parent and another child continued implementation and final delivery.
The parent and child inspected competing workspace state; the issue was not an available completed result being ignored.
There is no wait-to-timeout episode without inspection; actors continued probing, inspecting files, testing, and reconciling before finalization.
Competing implementation files existed, but a more specific same deliverable replacement is directly proven.
Two agents edited `compile.sh`, but the same episode also replaced the required executable/build entry point, so `Deliverable Overwrite` takes precedence.
The observed replacement targeted the build script and executable entry point, not a non-entry library or module source owned by another agent.

Multiple live parallel agents replaced the required build entry point and executable target: the parent added one `compile.sh`, a child observed that another agent had changed `compile.sh` and `./executable`, the child rewrote `compile.sh` to its own implementation, and the parent later found the executable already overwritten.
